learn.rule: A summary is one sentence. It tells who or what the text is about and the most important thing. Leave out tiny details and opinions.
learn.ruleEs: Un resumen es una sola oración. Dice de quién o de qué trata el texto y lo más importante. Deja fuera detalles pequeños y opiniones.
learn.model: Penguins are birds that cannot fly, but they are strong swimmers.
learn.notice: One sentence tells who the text is about and the big point. It does not list every fact.

items.prompt: Which sentence is the best summary of the octopus passage?
items.text: An octopus is a clever sea animal. It can squeeze through tiny spaces because it has no bones. An octopus can also change color to hide from enemies. One octopus at an aquarium opened a jar lid to get a snack.

options.text: An octopus is a clever sea animal that can squeeze through tiny spaces and change color.
One octopus opened a jar lid.
I think octopuses are the best animals in the sea.

items.why: A good summary names the animal and its most important facts. The jar lid is a tiny detail, and the last choice is an opinion.
items.whyEs: Un buen resumen nombra al animal y sus datos más importantes. La tapa del frasco es un detalle pequeño y la última opción es una opinión.

items.prompt: Which summary of the octopus passage is too long?
items.text: An octopus is a clever sea animal. It can squeeze through tiny spaces because it has no bones. An octopus can also change color to hide from enemies. One octopus at an aquarium opened a jar lid to get a snack.

options.text: An octopus is a clever sea animal that squeezes through tiny spaces and changes color.
Octopuses are animals.
An octopus is a clever sea animal that has no bones and squeezes through tiny spaces, and it changes color to hide, and one octopus at an aquarium opened a jar lid to get a snack.

items.why: A summary should be short. The long choice copies almost every sentence, including the tiny jar lid detail.
items.whyEs: Un resumen debe ser corto. La opción larga copia casi todas las oraciones, incluso el detalle pequeño de la tapa del frasco.

items.prompt: Check the details to cut from a one-sentence summary of the giraffe passage.
items.text: Giraffes are the tallest animals on land. Their long necks help them reach leaves high in trees. A giraffe's tongue is dark purple. My friend drew a giraffe in art class.

options.text: Giraffes are the tallest animals on land.
A giraffe's tongue is dark purple.
Their long necks help them reach leaves high in trees.
My friend drew a giraffe in art class.

items.why: Keep the main idea and the key fact about long necks. Cut the tiny detail about the tongue and the sentence about your friend.
items.whyEs: Conserva la idea principal y el dato clave sobre el cuello largo. Quita el detalle pequeño de la lengua y la oración sobre tu amigo.

items.prompt: Which summary of the Moon passage stays on the main idea?
items.text: The Moon travels around Earth. It does not make its own light. It shines because it reflects sunlight. People on Earth see it glow at night.

options.text: People like looking at the sky at night.
The Moon is round.
The Moon shines at night because it reflects sunlight.

items.why: The main idea is how the Moon shines. The first choice changes the focus to people, and the second is too small.
items.whyEs: La idea principal es cómo brilla la Luna. La primera opción cambia el enfoque a las personas y la segunda es muy pequeña.

items.prompt: Finish the summary frame for the octopus passage.
parts: An octopus is a clever sea animal that can
items.model: An octopus is a clever sea animal that can squeeze through tiny spaces and change color.
items.why: The words in a summary come from the most important facts in the text. The passage says the octopus squeezes and changes color.
items.whyEs: Las palabras de un resumen salen de los datos más importantes del texto. El texto dice que el pulpo se escurre y cambia de color.

write.prompt: Read the passage. Write one sentence that tells the main idea.
write.promptEs: Lee el texto. Escribe una oración que diga la idea principal.
write.text: Bats are the only mammals that can truly fly. Most bats sleep during the day and hunt at night. They use sound echoes to find insects in the dark. A bat can eat thousands of tiny insects in one night.

label: I named what the passage is about
Nombré de qué trata el texto
I included the most important idea
Incluí la idea más importante

write.model: Bats are flying mammals that hunt insects at night using sound echoes.

familyTalk.en: After a short video or story, each person tells it in one sentence.
familyTalk.es: Después de un video o un cuento corto, cada persona lo cuenta en una sola oración.

teacherTip.en: Have students cross out the tiny details in the passage first, then write the summary from what is left.
teacherTip.es: Pide que primero tachen los detalles pequeños del texto y luego escriban el resumen con lo que queda.

learn.rule: To summarize, find the most important idea and say it in one short sentence. Skip the small details.
learn.ruleEs: Para resumir, encuentra la idea más importante y dila en una oración corta. Omite los detalles pequeños.
learn.model: A library is a place where people borrow books for free.
learn.notice: The summary has a who or what and the key point. It is short and has no opinion.

items.prompt: Which sentence is the best summary of the one-room school passage?
items.text: Long ago, many children learned in a one-room schoolhouse. Students of all ages sat in the same room. One teacher taught every lesson. Children wrote on small slates instead of paper.

options.text: Children wrote on slates.
Long ago, children of all ages learned together in one room with one teacher.
I would not like to go to school in a small room.

items.why: The summary tells the big idea: who learned and how the school worked. Slates are a smaller detail, and the last choice is an opinion.
items.whyEs: El resumen dice la idea principal: quiénes aprendían y cómo funcionaba la escuela. Las pizarras son un detalle menor y la última opción es una opinión.

items.prompt: Which summary of the one-room school passage is too short?
items.text: Long ago, many children learned in a one-room schoolhouse. Students of all ages sat in the same room. One teacher taught every lesson. Children wrote on small slates instead of paper.

options.text: Children learned in one room with one teacher.
School.
Long ago, students of all ages shared one room and one teacher.

items.why: One word does not tell the reader what the passage says. A summary needs who or what and the key idea.
items.whyEs: Una sola palabra no dice lo que cuenta el texto. Un resumen necesita quién o qué y la idea clave.

items.prompt: Check the details to cut from a one-sentence summary of the farmers market passage.
items.text: A farmers market is a place where farmers sell food. Shoppers can buy fresh fruit, vegetables, and eggs. Some markets also have musicians. The market near my house opens on Saturdays.

options.text: A farmers market is a place where farmers sell food.
Shoppers can buy fresh fruit, vegetables, and eggs.
Some markets also have musicians.
The market near my house opens on Saturdays.

items.why: The summary keeps what a farmers market is and what shoppers buy. The musicians and your own market are extra details.
items.whyEs: El resumen conserva qué es un mercado de agricultores y qué compran las personas. Los músicos y tu propio mercado son detalles extra.

items.prompt: Which summary of the community passage has the right focus?
items.text: A community is a group of people who live and work in the same place. People in a community share parks, schools, and libraries. They also follow rules that keep everyone safe.

options.text: Parks are fun.
I live in a community with a library.
A community is a group of people who share a place and follow safe rules.

items.why: A good summary keeps the focus of the whole passage. The first choice is one small part, and the second choice is about the writer.
items.whyEs: Un buen resumen mantiene el enfoque de todo el texto. La primera opción es una parte pequeña y la segunda trata de quien escribe.

items.prompt: Finish the summary frame for the one-room school passage.
parts: learned together in one room with one
items.model: Long ago, children of all ages learned together in one room with one teacher.
items.why: The missing words are the key facts from the passage: students of all ages and one teacher.
items.whyEs: Las palabras que faltan son los datos clave del texto: estudiantes de todas las edades y un solo maestro.

write.prompt: Read the passage. Write one sentence that tells the main idea.
write.promptEs: Lee el texto. Escribe una oración que diga la idea principal.
write.text: Every state has a capital city. The capital is where leaders meet to make laws. Annapolis is the capital of Maryland. Many tourists like to visit its old buildings.
write.frame: A capital is the city where ___.

label: I named what the passage is about
Nombré de qué trata el texto
I included the most important idea
Incluí la idea más importante

write.model: A capital is the city where a state's leaders meet to make laws.

familyTalk.en: Read one short paragraph from a book or sign together. Say what it was about in one sentence.
familyTalk.es: Lean juntos un párrafo corto de un libro o de un letrero. Digan de qué trataba en una oración.

teacherTip.en: Ask students to hold up one finger when they hear the sentence that tells the most important idea.
teacherTip.es: Pide que levanten un dedo cuando oigan la oración que dice la idea más importante.

learn.rule: A math summary tells the big idea in one sentence. Keep the key words and leave out the small examples.
learn.ruleEs: Un resumen de matemáticas dice la idea principal en una oración. Conserva las palabras clave y deja fuera los ejemplos pequeños.
learn.model: A clock has two hands that show the hours and the minutes.
learn.notice: The summary names the thing and tells its main job. It does not repeat each fact.

items.prompt: Which sentence is the best summary of the fraction passage?
items.text: A fraction names equal parts of a whole. The bottom number tells how many equal parts there are. The top number tells how many of those parts we are talking about.

options.text: Fractions are the hardest math.
The top number is a number.
A fraction uses a top number and a bottom number to name equal parts of a whole.

items.why: The best summary names the main idea of the whole passage. One choice is an opinion and the other is too small.
items.whyEs: El mejor resumen nombra la idea principal de todo el texto. Una opción es una opinión y la otra es muy pequeña.

items.prompt: Which summary of the ruler passage is too long?
items.text: We measure length with a ruler. A ruler shows inches on one side. It shows centimeters on the other side. Line up the zero mark with one end of the object.

options.text: A ruler measures length in inches or centimeters.
We measure length with a ruler, which shows inches on one side and centimeters on the other side, and we line up the zero mark with one end of the object.
Rulers.

items.why: This summary copies almost every sentence of the passage. A summary should be much shorter than the text.
items.whyEs: Este resumen copia casi todas las oraciones del texto. Un resumen debe ser mucho más corto que el texto.

items.prompt: Check the details to cut from a one-sentence summary of the place value passage.
items.text: Our number system uses place value. The digit 4 in 42 means 4 tens. The digit 2 means 2 ones. I like the number 42 because it is my bus number. My teacher wore a blue shirt today.

options.text: Our number system uses place value.
The digit 4 in 42 means 4 tens.
I like the number 42 because it is my bus number.
The digit 2 means 2 ones.
My teacher wore a blue shirt today.

items.why: The summary keeps place value and what the digits mean. The bus number and the blue shirt are small details that do not help explain place value.
items.whyEs: El resumen conserva el valor posicional y lo que significan los dígitos. El número del autobús y la camisa azul son detalles pequeños que no ayudan a explicarlo.

items.prompt: Which summary of the ruler passage has the right focus?
items.text: We measure length with a ruler. A ruler shows inches on one side. It shows centimeters on the other side. Line up the zero mark with one end of the object.

options.text: Rulers are good.
A ruler shows inches on one side and centimeters on the other side.
My ruler is long and has numbers on it.

items.why: This summary keeps the key facts about what a ruler shows. The first choice is vague and the last choice is about the writer's ruler.
items.whyEs: Este resumen conserva los datos clave de lo que muestra una regla. La primera opción es vaga y la última trata de la regla de quien escribe.

items.prompt: Finish the summary frame for the fraction passage.
items.model: A fraction names equal parts of a whole.
items.why: The key words of the passage are equal parts and whole. The summary uses them in one short sentence.
items.whyEs: Las palabras clave del texto son equal parts y whole. El resumen las usa en una oración corta.

write.prompt: Read the passage. Write one sentence that tells the main idea.
write.promptEs: Lee el texto. Escribe una oración que diga la idea principal.
write.text: A shape with four straight sides is a quadrilateral. A square, a rectangle, and a rhombus are quadrilaterals. Their sides are straight and they close up with no gaps. Some quadrilaterals have four square corners.

label: I named what the passage is about
Nombré de qué trata el texto
I included the most important idea

write.model: Quadrilaterals are closed shapes with four straight sides, like squares and rectangles.

familyTalk.en: Ask your child to explain one thing they learned in math today in just one sentence.
familyTalk.es: Pidan a su hijo o hija que explique en una sola oración algo que aprendió hoy en matemáticas.

teacherTip.en: Have students underline the key math words in the passage, then use two of them in the summary.
teacherTip.es: Pide que subrayen las palabras clave de matemáticas del texto y usen dos de ellas en el resumen.
